newsitem.title: UK: BA agrees to pay holiday firm for delays.
newsitem.headline: BA agrees to pay holiday firm for delays.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday that it agreed to pay 1.6 million stg to Inspirations Plc's unit Caledonian Airways and invest 4.4 million stg in Inspirations to settle a claim on aircraft maintenance work.
Inspirations issued a profit warning in October saying its 1996 results had been hit by the costs of disruption to its flights caused by delays in aircraft maintenance work.
A BA statement said there were several occasions this summer when aircraft were returned to Caledonian behind schedule after engineering work.

"BA regards Caledonian Airways as a valued customer and will enhance its engineering support...by dedicating engineering reosurces specifically to the Caledonian (Lockheed) Tristar fleet. At the same time a mutually acceptable schedule of maintenance activity has been agreed," the statement said.

"British Airways Engineering has acknowledged that there were occasions when engineering work had taken longer than anticipated, but safety is paramount and neither Caledonian Airways or British Airways would ever allow safety to be compromised."
Caledonian was sold by BA to Inspirations in 1995.
